evidence: The paper uses random forest as one of six classifiers tested (section 3.6: "random forest (RF) [ 40 ]") but reports only classification accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity (Table 1: RF achieved 0.989 accuracy) with no impurity-based importance measures. Feature interpretation relies instead on marginal relevance scores ("MR score for each wavelength is the ratio of the between-class to within-class sum of squares") and PCA loadings. Conclusions address classification performance and system throughput, not variable importance ranking.
